# Search index + mindmap synthesis reference

Reference for the two cross-cutting content features that get added to the build script when growing a static study site from one chapter to many: auto mindmap synthesis for chapters whose source MDs lack explicit mermaid blocks, and universal search across all topics via a flat JSON index.

## 1. Auto mindmap synthesis from headings

**Problem.** The renderer fires `render_mindmap_md()` only when an explicit `mermaid` / `mindmap` / `flowchart` code block is present in the source MD. Older chapters, or chapters generated by agents that don't emit mermaid, render as plain text — no visual hierarchy. After a "make mindmaps work on all chapters" request, only the chapters whose source MDs had mermaid blocks actually got visuals.

**Solution.** Add a synthesis fallback to the build script's `render_md_to_html()`. If no mermaid block was rendered, extract H1/H2/H3 from the source MD and synthesize a mindmap from them.

```python
def _synthesize_mindmap_from_headings(md_text: str) -> str:
    headings = []
    for line in md_text.split("\n"):
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*$", line)
        if m:
            level = len(m.group(1))
            text = re.sub(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*", r"\1", m.group(2).strip())
            text = re.sub(r"\*(.+?)\*", r"\1", text)
            text = re.sub(r"`(.+?)`", r"\1", text)
            if len(text) > 80:
                text = text[:77] + "..."
            headings.append((level, text))
    if len(headings) < 2:
        return ""
    root = ""
    items = []
    for lvl, txt in headings[:40]:
        if lvl == 1 and not root:
            root = txt
            continue
        if lvl in (2, 3):
            items.append((lvl, txt))
    if not root and items:
        root = items.pop(0)[1]
    if not root:
        return ""
    lines = ["mindmap", f"  root(({root}))"]
    for lvl, txt in items[:30]:
        indent = "    " if lvl == 2 else "      "
        lines.append(f"{indent}{txt}")
    return render_mindmap_md("\n".join(lines))


def render_md_to_html(md_text: str) -> str:
    # ... existing parser setup ...
    found_mermaid = False  # NEW

    def flush_code():
        nonlocal in_code, code_buf, code_kind, code_fence_open, found_mermaid  # NEW
        if not in_code: return
        body = "\n".join(code_buf)
        if code_kind in ("mindmap",):
            rendered = render_mindmap_md(body)
            found_mermaid = True                  # NEW
        elif code_kind in ("flowchart", "graph"):
            rendered = render_flowchart_md(body)
            found_mermaid = True                  # NEW
        else:
            rendered = f'<pre class="codeblock"><code>{_esc(body)}</code></pre>'
        out.append(rendered)
        in_code = False; code_buf = []; code_kind = None; code_fence_open = None

    # ... existing line loop ...
    flush_list(); flush_table(); flush_code()

    # NEW: synthesize if no explicit block was found
    if not found_mermaid:
        synth = _synthesize_mindmap_from_headings(md_text)
        if synth:
            out.append('<h2>Topic Overview</h2>')
            out.append(synth)
    return "\n".join(out)
```

**Verification (per-chapter coverage):**

```python
import json
for d in sorted(site.glob("[0-9]*-*/")):
    p = d / "topics.json"
    if not p.exists(): continue
    data = json.load(open(p))
    synth = sum(1 for t in data["topics"] if "Topic Overview" in t["html"])
    expl  = sum(1 for t in data["topics"] if 'class="mindmap"' in t["html"] and "Topic Overview" not in t["html"])
    total = len(data["topics"])
    print(f"{d.name:50s} {total:4d} topics | {expl:3d} explicit + {synth:3d} synthesized")
```

**What synthesis produces (Ch 32 example).** For a topic MD that has H1 = "Ageing definition" and H2s = "Core Clinical Content", "FCPS/MRCP High-Yield Summary", "Viva Questions", etc., the synthesized mindmap looks like:

```html
<div class="mindmap">
  <div class="mm-root">Ageing definition</div>
  <div class="mm-branches">
    <div class="mm-branch">
      <div class="mm-node mm-l1">Core Clinical Content</div>
      <div class="mm-node mm-l2">Ageing definition</div>
      <div class="mm-node mm-l2">Population trends</div>
      <div class="mm-node mm-l2">Theories of ageing</div>
      <div class="mm-node mm-l2">Telomere shortening</div>
      ...
    </div>
    <div class="mm-branch"><div class="mm-node mm-l1">FCPS/MRCP High-Yield Summary</div></div>
    ...
  </div>
</div>
```

Identical styling to explicitly-authored mindmaps, so the user can't tell which is which from the rendered page. The verification probe (counting `"Topic Overview"` strings) is the only way to know.

**Edge cases where synthesis silently fails:**
- Topic with H1 only (no H2/H3) — `len(headings) < 2` check returns `""`
- Topic with H1 = "Definition" and H2 = "FCPS/MRCP High-Yield Summary" (no actual content between) — synthesis still works, just produces a shallow mindmap
- Pure-table topic (no headings) — synthesis returns `""` and the topic renders as a table only

These are acceptable. Don't add LLM-based synthesis to "fix" them — the visual would be low quality and the cost is high.

## 2. Universal search via search_index.json

**Problem.** The chapter SPA has a sidebar filter (hides topics within the current chapter). With 32 chapters and 2,957 topics, the user needs to find any topic from any chapter without first opening the chapter page. Sidebar filter doesn't help — it's per-chapter.

**Solution.** Generate a flat JSON index at build time, expose it as `/search_index.json`, add a header input that lazy-loads the index on first keystroke and renders a dropdown of scored matches with keyboard navigation.

### Build side

```python
def write_search_index(site_data):
    items = []
    for ch_slug, (ch_name, _ch_url, _ch_color) in BUILT_CHAPTERS.items():
        info = site_data.get(ch_slug)
        if not info or info["n_topics"] == 0:
            continue
        ch_num = ch_slug.split("-")[0]
        for hub_num in sorted(info["by_hub"].keys()):
            hub_topics = sorted(info["by_hub"][hub_num], key=lambda t: t["local_prefix"])
            hub_name = info["hub_names"].get(hub_num, hub_num)
            for t in hub_topics:
                title = t["slug"].replace("-", " ").title()
                items.append({
                    "chapter_num": ch_num,
                    "chapter_name": ch_name,
                    "chapter_slug": ch_slug,
                    "hub_num": hub_num,
                    "hub_name": hub_name,
                    "topic": t["local_prefix"],
                    "title": title,
                    "url": f"/{ch_slug}/",
                })
    (SITE / "search_index.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(items, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    )
    print(f"  Wrote search_index.json ({len(items)} topics)")
```

For 2,957 topics this produces a ~700KB JSON. One fetch on first keystroke, then cached in the page's `idx` variable. Use `separators=(",", ":")` to drop unnecessary whitespace.

### Client side (vanilla JS, no library)

```html
<div class="search-box" id="searchBox">
  <input type="text" id="searchInput" placeholder="Search 2,957 topics…"
         autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
  <div class="search-results" id="searchResults"></div>
</div>
```

```javascript
(function() {
  let idx = null, debounce = null;
  const input = document.getElementById('searchInput');
  const results = document.getElementById('searchResults');
  const box = document.getElementById('searchBox');

  function loadIdx() {
    if (idx) return Promise.resolve(idx);
    return fetch('/search_index.json').then(r => r.json()).then(d => { idx = d; return d; });
  }

  function esc(s) { return s.replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/>/g,'&gt;'); }
  function highlight(text, q) {
    const i = text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q.toLowerCase());
    if (i < 0) return esc(text);
    return esc(text.slice(0,i)) + '<mark>' + esc(text.slice(i,i+q.length)) + '</mark>' + esc(text.slice(i+q.length));
  }

  function search(q) {
    loadIdx().then(data => {
      const ql = q.toLowerCase();
      const hits = [];
      for (const item of data) {
        const t = item.title.toLowerCase(), h = item.hub_name.toLowerCase(), c = item.chapter_name.toLowerCase();
        let s = 0;
        if      (t === ql)                              s = 100;
        else if (t.startsWith(ql))                      s = 80;
        else if (t.includes(ql))                        s = 60;
        else if (item.topic && item.topic.startsWith(ql)) s = 70;
        else if (h.includes(ql))                        s = 40;
        else if (c.includes(ql))                        s = 20;
        if (s > 0) hits.push({item, score: s});
      }
      hits.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || a.item.title.localeCompare(b.item.title));
      const top = hits.slice(0, 20);
      results.innerHTML = top.length === 0
        ? '<div class="search-empty">No topics match "<strong>' + esc(q) + '</strong>"</div>'
        : top.map(h => '<a class="search-hit" href="' + h.item.url + '?topic=' + encodeURIComponent(h.item.topic) + '">'
            + '<span class="hit-ch">' + h.item.chapter_num + '</span>'
            + '<span class="hit-body">'
              + '<span class="hit-title">' + highlight(h.item.title, q) + '</span>'
              + '<span class="hit-meta">' + highlight(h.item.chapter_name, q) + ' · ' + highlight(h.item.hub_name, q) + ' · ' + h.item.topic + '</span>'
            + '</span>'
            + '<span class="hit-arrow">→</span>'
          + '</a>').join('');
      if (hits.length > 20) results.innerHTML += '<div class="search-more">+' + (hits.length - 20) + ' more matches…</div>';
      box.classList.add('open');
    });
  }

  input.addEventListener('input', e => {
    clearTimeout(debounce);
    const q = e.target.value.trim();
    if (q.length < 2) { results.innerHTML = ''; box.classList.remove('open'); return; }
    debounce = setTimeout(() => search(q), 120);
  });
  document.addEventListener('click', e => { if (!box.contains(e.target)) box.classList.remove('open'); });
  input.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') { input.value = ''; results.innerHTML = ''; box.classList.remove('open'); input.blur(); return; }
    const hits = results.querySelectorAll('.search-hit');
    let ai = Array.from(hits).findIndex(h => h.classList.contains('active'));
    if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') { e.preventDefault(); ai = Math.min(ai + 1, hits.length - 1); }
    else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') { e.preventDefault(); ai = Math.max(ai - 1, 0); }
    else if (e.key === 'Enter' && hits[ai]) { e.preventDefault(); hits[ai].click(); return; }
    hits.forEach((h, i) => h.classList.toggle('active', i === ai));
  });
})();
```

@media (max-width: 720px) { header.site .search-box { max-width: 180px; } }

### Common bugs

- **`position: absolute` for the dropdown** — clipped by sidebar overflow. Use `position: fixed; top: 56px;` instead.
- **Loading the index on every page load** — wasteful. Lazy-load on first input keystroke only.
- **No keyboard nav** — only mouse works. The user will complain within 30s. Add ↑/↓/Enter/Escape.
- **Highlighting breaks the layout** — `<mark>` adds background. Use `background: rgba(56,189,248,0.25)` not a solid block color.
- **Search index in JS bundle** — kills the cache benefit. Keep it a separate `.json` request.
- **URL `?topic=` doesn't load the right topic on click** — the SPA must read the `topic` query param on `loadManifest()` and call `showTopic(t)`. The hit link is `<href>?topic=<local_prefix>` so the chapter SPA boots with the right topic selected.

## 3. Docker port alignment bug (and how to spot it fast)

**Symptom:** Container is running (`docker ps` shows it) but `curl http://localhost:<host_port>/` returns `Connection reset by peer` or `Empty reply from server`. Container status is `unhealthy`. `docker exec <name> wget http://127.0.0.1:80/` succeeds; `wget http://127.0.0.1:<host_port>/` fails.

**Cause:** Someone wrote `listen <host_port>` in `docker/nginx.conf` instead of `listen 80`. The host `-p <host_port>:80` maps the host port to container port 80, but nginx is listening on `<host_port>` instead of 80. So nothing is bound on 80 (where the host maps to) and the `<host_port>` listening socket is unreachable from outside the container network namespace.

**Fix:**

```nginx
server {
    listen 80;                    # always 80, regardless of host port
    server_name _;
    # ... rest of config
}
```

```dockerfile
EXPOSE 80                       # always 80
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s \
  CMD wget -q --spider http://localhost/ || exit 1     # http://localhost/, not localhost:<port>
```

**Diagnostic check after every docker build:**

```bash
docker run -d --name <name> -p <host_port>:80 <image>
sleep 2
docker exec <name> wget -q -O- http://127.0.0.1:80/ | head -1   # should return HTML
curl -sI http://localhost:<host_port>/ | head -1                  # should return HTTP/1.1 200
```

If the in-container `wget` succeeds but the host `curl` fails, the nginx config has the wrong `listen` port. If both fail, the nginx config has a syntax error — `docker logs <name>` for the error.

**Why this bug recurs:** the host port is configured in three places — `EXPOSE`, `listen`, and the `-p` flag. It's tempting to "be consistent" by setting all three to the same port. But `EXPOSE` and `listen` are inside-container, `-p` is the host-side port mapping. The two namespaces must agree on 80, the host port is decoupled. Setting `listen 8855` "matches" the host port but breaks the `-p 8855:80` mapping.

## 4. Verification standard for cross-cutting changes

After ANY change to `build_site.py` that affects more than one topic (synthesis, search, new CSS, new pitfall), the verification must include **per-chapter coverage**, not a single spot check:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
site = Path("site")

# Example: mindmap coverage
print("Chapter                       | Topics | Explicit | Synthesized | Total with mindmap")
print("-" * 90)
totals = [0, 0, 0, 0]
for d in sorted(site.glob("[0-9]*-*/")):
    p = d / "topics.json"
    if not p.exists(): continue
    data = json.load(open(p))
    total = len(data["topics"])
    expl  = sum(1 for t in data["topics"] if 'class="mindmap"' in t["html"] and "Topic Overview" not in t["html"])
    synth = sum(1 for t in data["topics"] if "Topic Overview" in t["html"])
    covered = expl + synth
    print(f"{d.name:50s} | {total:4d}  |   {expl:3d}   |     {synth:3d}      |      {covered:3d}")
    totals[0] += total; totals[1] += expl; totals[2] += synth; totals[3] += covered
print("-" * 90)
print(f"{'TOTAL':50s} | {totals[0]:4d}  |   {totals[1]:3d}   |     {totals[2]:3d}      |      {totals[3]:3d}")
```

Expected output for the MedSea site after synthesis is enabled (32 chapters, 2,957 topics):

```
Chapter                       | Topics | Explicit | Synthesized | Total with mindmap
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1-clinical-decision-making    |    6   |     0    |      6      |       6
10-acute-medicine             |   43   |     2    |     41      |      43
16-cardiology                 |  330   |     0    |    328      |     328
19-clinical-biochemistry      |   28   |    28    |      0      |      28
...
TOTAL                         | 2957   |   401    |   2203      |    2604
```

If a chapter shows `0 synthesized` and `0 explicit` when it has 50+ topics, the synthesis is broken for that chapter — investigate the source MDs (probably unnumbered headers, no H1, or pure-table content).

**Do not declare done after one chapter passes.** The user has been burned by this multiple times — assistant reports "synthesis works" after testing on Ch 19 (which has explicit mermaid blocks) without verifying the other 31 chapters (most of which lack explicit blocks). Always run the per-chapter table.
